_comment: Small curated MITRE ATT&CK (Enterprise) subset, each with short match keywords rather than full-text retrieval — this project's RAG counterpart lives in ioc-triage-assistant. For production use, sync against https://github.com/mitre-attack/attack-stix-data.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.text: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell for execution, often with base64-encoded commands to evade static detection.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.text: Adversaries may dump credentials from LSASS memory or the SAM database using tools like Mimikatz to obtain account hashes and passwords.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.text: Adversaries may transfer additional tools into a compromised environment, often via HTTP downloads disguised as legitimate traffic.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job
techniques.text: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling to establish persistence after initial access.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.text: Adversaries, commonly ransomware operators, delete shadow copies and backups to prevent recovery before encrypting data.

techniques.name: Create Account
techniques.text: Adversaries may create or modify local accounts and group membership to maintain access.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.text: Adversaries may use compromised credentials for legitimate accounts to blend in with normal activity, often visible as a login from an unexpected host.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.text: Adversaries may use application-layer protocols to blend command-and-control traffic with legitimate network traffic.

techniques.name: Proxy
techniques.text: Adversaries may route C2 traffic through Tor exit nodes or other proxies to obscure its true source or destination.
